text: Developmental Coordination Disorder (DCD) is a common neurodevelopmental condition characterized by impaired motor coordination, poor balance, reduced participation in physical activities, and limitations in functional performance. Conventional rehabilitation often requires prolonged therapist supervision and may not be consistently accessible, particularly in resource-limited settings. Parent-led rehabilitation and artificial intelligence (AI)-based movement analysis have emerged as promising approaches to enhance motor outcomes; however, evidence integrating these strategies remains limited. This manuscript presents the protocol for a randomized controlled trial evaluating a structured Parent-Led Neuromotor Training Programme integrated with AI-based movement analysis in children with DCD.
source_label: Development, validation and effectiveness of a parents led neuromotor training module with AI-based movement analysis for improving motor proficiency and sports participation in children with developmental coordination disorder: a protocol for an assessor-blinded randomized superiority controlled trial
